Play a word-guessing game: each guessed letter reveals every place it stands in the secret word, and ten failures lose the game.

Adapted from Exercism's [problem specification](https://github.com/exercism/problem-specifications/tree/main/exercises/save-the-cow) (MIT). Listed under [Games & Simulation](/examples/?subject=games-and-simulation).

```nomi-run
// FILE: save_the_cow.nomi
/// Where a game stands.
pub enum State {
    Ongoing
    Win
    Lose
}

derive Equatable for State

/// A guess the game no longer takes.
pub enum Error {
    AlreadyWon
    AlreadyLost
}

impl Display for Error {
    fn to_string(error: Error) -> String {
        case error {
            .AlreadyWon -> "cannot guess after the game is won"
            .AlreadyLost -> "cannot guess after the game is lost"
        }
    }
}

/// How many failures a game allows before the one that loses it.
once allowed_failures = 9

/// A word-guessing game. It is a value: each guess answers the game after
/// it.
pub opaque struct Game {
    word: List<Codepoint>
    revealed: Set<Codepoint>
    remaining_failures: Int
    state: State
}

impl Game {
    /// A new game whose secret is `word`, with no letters revealed.
    pub fn new(word: String) -> Game {
        #Game{
            word: String.to_codepoints(word),
            revealed: %[],
            remaining_failures: allowed_failures,
            state: .Ongoing,
        }
    }

    /// The game after guessing `letter`. A letter of the word not yet
    /// revealed reveals every place it stands; any other guess is a failure,
    /// and a failure with none remaining loses.
    pub fn guess(game: Game, letter: Codepoint) -> Result<Game, Error> {
        case game.state {
            .Win -> Err(.AlreadyWon)
            .Lose -> Err(.AlreadyLost)
            .Ongoing when hidden?(game, letter) -> Ok(reveal(game, letter))
            .Ongoing when game.remaining_failures == 0 -> Ok(#{..game, state: .Lose})
            .Ongoing -> Ok(#{..game, remaining_failures: game.remaining_failures - 1})
        }
    }

    /// Where the game stands.
    pub fn state(game: Game) -> State {
        game.state
    }

    /// The word with each letter not yet revealed written as `_`.
    pub fn masked_word(game: Game) -> String {
        game.word
        |> Iter.map(fn letter -> {
            if Set.contains?(game.revealed, letter) {
                letter
            } else {
                '_'
            }
        })
        |> Iter.to_list()
        |> String.from_codepoints()
    }

    /// How many more failures the game allows before the one that loses it.
    pub fn remaining_failures(game: Game) -> Int {
        game.remaining_failures
    }
}

/// Whether `letter` is in the word and not yet revealed.
fn hidden?(game: Game, letter: Codepoint) -> Bool {
    List.contains?(game.word, letter) and !Set.contains?(game.revealed, letter)
}

/// `game` with `letter` revealed, won when that reveals the whole word.
fn reveal(game: Game, letter: Codepoint) -> Game {
    revealed = Set.insert(game.revealed, letter)
    won = Iter.all?(game.word, &Set.contains?(revealed, &1))

    #{..game, revealed, state: if won { .Win } else { .Ongoing }}
}

// FILE: save_the_cow_test.nomi
import save_the_cow.{Error, Game, State}

/// A new game of `word` after each of `guesses` in turn, or the first
/// guess it refuses.
fn play(word: String, guesses: List<Codepoint>) -> Result<Game, Error> {
    Iter.reduce(guesses, fn game = Ok(Game.new(word)), letter -> {
        Result.flat_map(game, &Game.guess(&1, letter))
    })
}

test "guess" {
    cases: List<#(String, List<Codepoint>, State, String, Int)> = [
        #("Initially 9 failures are allowed and no letters are guessed", [], .Ongoing, "____", 9),
        #(
            "After 10 failures the game is over",
            ['a', 'b', 'c', 'd', 'e', 'f', 'g', 'h', 'i', 'j'],
            .Lose,
            "____",
            0,
        ),
        #(
            "Losing with several correct guesses",
            ['t', 'o', 'a', 'b', 'c', 'd', 'e', 'f', 'g', 'h', 'i', 'j'],
            .Lose,
            "_oot",
            0,
        ),
        #("Feeding a correct letter removes underscores", ['t'], .Ongoing, "___t", 9),
        #("Feeding a correct letter twice counts as a failure", ['t', 't'], .Ongoing, "___t", 8),
        #("Guessing a repeated letter reveals all instances", ['t', 't', 'o'], .Ongoing, "_oot", 8),
        #("Getting all the letters right makes for a win", ['t', 't', 'o', 'l'], .Win, "loot", 8),
        #(
            "Winning on the last guess is still a win",
            ['a', 'b', 'c', 'd', 'e', 'f', 'g', 'h', 'i', 't', 'o', 'l'],
            .Win,
            "loot",
            0,
        ),
    ]

    subtests cases, #(description, guesses, state, masked_word, remaining_failures), description {
        assert Ok(game) = play("loot", guesses)
        assert Game.state(game) == state
        assert Game.masked_word(game) == masked_word
        assert Game.remaining_failures(game) == remaining_failures
    }
}

test "guessing after the game is over" {
    cases = [
        #(
            "Guessing after a lose is error",
            ['a', 'b', 'c', 'd', 'e', 'f', 'g', 'h', 'i', 'j', 'k'],
            "cannot guess after the game is lost",
        ),
        #(
            "Guessing after a win is error",
            ['t', 'o', 'l', 'l'],
            "cannot guess after the game is won",
        ),
    ]

    subtests cases, #(description, guesses, message), description {
        assert Err(error) = play("loot", guesses)
        assert "${error}" == message
    }
}
```

## How it's written

- Adapted: the canonical comments suggest an object that changes with each guess, or a functional reactive design. The Nomi version is a value: `Game.guess` answers the game after the guess, and a sequence of guesses is a fold.
- `Game` is an opaque struct of the word's letters, the set of revealed letters, the failures remaining and the `State`. `guess` is one `case` on the state, with `when` guards for the ongoing game: a letter in the word and not yet revealed reveals it, any other guess (a wrong letter, or a right one guessed again) is a failure, and a failure with none remaining loses. The canonical counts fix that rule: 9 failures remain at the start, 0 after nine and still 0 after the tenth, which loses.
- Guessing after the game is over is an `Err`, one `Error` variant per outcome, whose `Display` gives the canonical messages.
- A guess is a `Codepoint`, since the game works letter by letter (style §19), and `masked_word` maps each letter of the word to itself or `_`.
- The test file's `play` folds the guesses over `Result.flat_map`, so the first refused guess is the answer. The cases are two `subtests` tables, one for the games that end in a state and one for the refused guesses.
